children.name: Oopelta capensis Pollonera, 1909
children.description:
External: Green-yellow to green-gray body, spots and lines of red-brown on dorsum and sides; greyish white body in alcohol; black spots on the mantle and dorsum of some specimens, others have just tiny dark spots on mantle and sometimes dorsum and sides; red-brown granules on mantle; pale foot fringe; sole and head yellowish or green-gray; eggs 3-3.5 mm diameter; blue-green slime (!) and possible reddish slime when irritated (van Bruggen in Altena 1966; Altena 1966).

Internal: Calcium carbonate granules as vestigial shell; no apparent epiphallus; large atrium (Altena 1966).

children.name: Ariostralis nebulosa Sirgel, 1985
children.description:
External: Black, dark gray, or brown-gray body; rounded backside without keel; hexagonal tubercles on skin; clear, sticky mucus; 1-part sole, body width or wider, remaining wide and flat when the animal is contracted (Sirgel 1985).

Internal: Internal shell 4.0 x 2.2. mm; pigmented ovotestis; penis with four sections: short basal apical section attached to vas deferens and retractor muscle and with an internal papilla, wider section and third sections containing calcareous spines with one very large spine, and fourth, basal section long and thin; vagina and oviduct longer than atrium; upper portion of vagina in the shape of a bulb, attached to spermatheca duct; vaginal bulb with a second inner cartilaginous wall attached by strands to outer wall; long spermatheca duct passes around base of retractor muscles and to albumen gland; very short atrium (Sirgel 1985).

children.name: Ariopelta capensis
children.description: Ariopelta capensis is a species of air-breathing land slug, a terrestrial, pulmonate, gastropod mollusc in the family Oopeltidae.
